reasons: Lake identity record is verified for Mitchell v. Wisconsin, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2019-06-27.

defect.evidence_quote: When police have probable cause to believe a person has committed a drunk-driving offense and the driver's unconsciousness or stupor requires him to be taken to the hospital or similar facility before police have a reasonable opportunity to administer a standard evidentiary breath test, they may almost always order a warrantless blood test to measure the driver's BAC without offending the Fourth Amendment.

defect.problem: The pin-2539 payload/lake pinpoint quote is not the opinion quote; it is generated page-header/background text and the lake itself flags quote_fidelity as mismatch. The actual displayed Rule quote in content_page.md is present verbatim in the opinion text, but the quote-pinpoint record under review is wrong.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace pin-2539's stored quote with the actual first sentence of text paragraph p-58, set the reporter page/pin metadata to 139 S. Ct. 2539 or equivalent, and clear the mismatch only after exact quote normalization.

reasons: The content-page Rule quote is character-faithful to text paragraph p-58.

residual_risks: Do not remove the displayed Rule quote solely because the lake pin record is bad; the displayed quote itself is verified from the disclosed text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Store only the opinion sentence in the pinpoint quote field; keep page-title, treatment, and background prose out of pinpoints.

reasons: The treatment payload fields match the lake treatment fields: good_law, as_of_content 2019-06-27, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the same plurality/concurrence scope note.
Treatment/currency merits are outside lens A, so no treatment finding is raised.
